[ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r9] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | When he falls into the pit, dies, or is destroyed, his wealth cannot rescue him from the grave or ruin and instead increases his punishment and loss.
[QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r1] QUTB-ZILAL, d. 1386 · author | holds | At the end of repeated stumbles and deviations, wealth hoarded or used to replace God and guidance cannot help its owner. | mentions 92:8
[QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r2] QUTB-ZILAL, d. 1386 · author | holds | Being enabled in sin is the hard path even if its owner prospers in this world; nothing is harder than Hell, which is the ultimate hardship. | mentions 92:10
[QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r3] QUTB-ZILAL, d. 1386 · author | holds | Across all times and places there are two paths, parties, and standards beneath many outward forms; each person chooses, and God facilitates that chosen route.
[QUTB-ZILAL:92:11/r4] QUTB-ZILAL, d. 1386 · author | holds | The next section describes each group’s end and first establishes that each outcome is just, true, and inevitable.
[IBNASHUR:92:11/r1] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | This clause coordinates with the promise of facilitation to al-ʿusrā and means God will hasten him to Hell; the implied phrase is when he falls into it. | mentions 92:10
[IBNASHUR:92:11/r2] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Al-taraddī is falling from a height to a lower place; here the miser's wealth will not avert any of the Fire's punishment.
[IBNASHUR:92:11/r3] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Mā can be negative, yielding the prediction that his wealth will not benefit him when he falls into Hell.
[IBNASHUR:92:11/r4] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Alternatively, mā is an interrogative of rebuke, and on this reading the initial wāw may begin a new sentence: what will his hoarded wealth avail him?
[IBNASHUR:92:11/r5] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās relates that a hypocrite took fallen dates from a poor Muslim's children; after the Prophet's offer of a palm in Paradise was refused, Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought the tree for an orchard of forty palms and gave it to the family.
[IBNASHUR:92:11/r6] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās attributes revelation of Sūrat al-Layl through al-ʿusrā to the story; the report is described as gharīb, and some scholars consequently called the sūra Medinan.
[IBNASHUR:92:11/r7] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · author | holds | Ibn ʿĀshūr cautions that early scholars often used 'revealed concerning this' to mean a story is covered by a verse, not that it occasioned revelation; he applies that convention here.
[IBNASHUR:92:11/r8] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | A report says the Prophet praised the many luxuriant date clusters awaiting Abū al-Daḥdāḥ in Paradise.
[IBNASHUR:92:11/r9] IBNASHUR, d. 1393 · بشار بن برد | reports | Bashshār ibn Burd alludes to the episode in a line about the little palm bending; al-nuḥayla is the poetic image for the tree.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The preceding surah swore by the soul's shaping, meaning the creation of intellect and knowledge; this surah swears by the human body and its sexes. The oath's response is that human efforts differ, with the emphasis on wealth failing in the fall.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p380/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | سعي literally means brisk, forceful walking and is metaphorically used for work and striving.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Verse 11 coordinates with the preceding promise: wealth withheld will not help when its owner falls into Hell; تردى means falling from a height to a depth. | mentions 92:10
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | reports | ما may be a negation or a rhetorical question of rebuke; on the latter reading, the waw can introduce a new sentence.
[TABATABAI:92:8-13/r3] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Tarradda is falling from a height and by extension destruction; the fall may be into the grave, Hell, or simply death. The question asks what his wealth could do, or states that it will do nothing.
[ASAD-NOTES:92:8#n6/r1] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | The phrase may be rendered as a statement: his wealth will be of no avail when he falls.
[BINTSHATI:v2p106/r1] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · author | holds | The contrast concerns giving away wealth and hoarding it: the passage says the miser's wealth will not help him and describes the giver as giving wealth to purify himself. | mentions 92:11, 92:18
[BINTSHATI:v2p109/r3] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · author | holds | Ghina can mean self-sufficiency even without wealth, while thara denotes possession of wealth unless used figuratively. | mentions 93:8
[BINTSHATI:v2p109/r4] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · author | holds | Rada originally means destruction and includes the physical image of a rock or falling into a well, then extends to ruin generally.
[BINTSHATI:v2p110/r1] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · author | holds | Taradda is the intransitive form of arda, to destroy or cause ruin; the Quran uses the root in related forms for perishing, causing ruin, and a fallen animal, and this exhausts its occurrences. | mentions 20:15-16, 41:23, 37:56, 6:137, 5:3
[BINTSHATI:v2p110/r2] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · author | prefers | The author understands taradda as plunging into ruin and prefers al-Tabari's reading as falling into Hell over the reported burial-shroud reading.
[BINTSHATI:v2p110/r3] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · أبو حيان | reports | Abu Hayyan transmits the alternative reading of taradda as being covered by a burial shroud, supported by lines from Malik ibn al-Rayb and another poet.
[BINTSHATI:v2p110/r4] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · author | rejects | The shroud reading does not fit the warning against the miser, since death in a shroud applies to believers as well as disbelievers.
[BINTSHATI:v2p111/r5] BINTSHATI, d. 1419 · author | prefers | The author prefers the negative parsing of ma because it emphatically states that wealth cannot help the miser when he falls into ruin.
[BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p374/r1] BINTSHATI-IJAZ, d. 1419 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas glosses tarda as dying and falling into Hell; he cites a line by Adi ibn Zayd about a man struck by death while expecting a long reign.
[BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r1] BINTSHATI-IJAZ, d. 1419 · ابن الأثير | reports | Ibn al-Athīr glosses the hadith’s “causes him to fall” as bringing a person into ruin.
[BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r2] BINTSHATI-IJAZ, d. 1419 · ابن عباس | prefers | Ibn ʿAbbās interprets tarradā as falling into Hell, an Islamic contextual sense supported by the warning immediately afterward and by 37:56 and 41:22. | mentions 92:14, 92:15, 92:16, 37:55, 37:56, 41:22
[BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p375/r3] BINTSHATI-IJAZ, d. 1419 · author | rejects | The author rejects ʿAdī ibn Zayd’s poetic line as evidence for the specifically Islamic sense of falling into Hell; its explicit context points instead to falling to death.
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:11:anmerkung/r1] CORPUSCORANICUM · Bergsträßer | reports | Mā can be read either as a question pronoun or as a negation particle.
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:11:anmerkung/r2] CORPUSCORANICUM · author | prefers | The negation is more likely here; the commentary points to 111:2 and two biblical intertexts. | mentions 111:2
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1] CORPUSCORANICUM · author | holds | The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17. | mentions 92:5, 92:6, 92:7, 92:8, 92:9, 92:10, 92:11, 92:17, 92:18, 92:19, 92:20
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2] CORPUSCORANICUM · author | holds | The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior li

sts precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct. | mentions 92:5, 92:6, 92:7, 92:8, 92:9, 92:10, 92:11, 92:14, 92:15, 92:16, 92:17, 92:18, 92:19, 92:20
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1] CORPUSCORANICUM · author | holds | The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6] CORPUSCORANICUM · Neuwirth | reports | Neuwirth classifies verse 11 with the theological predication in verses 12–13 rather than with the preceding description of the wicked. | mentions 92:12, 92:13
[CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r7] CORPUSCORANICUM · author | prefers | Verse 11 belongs with the wicked person's section because its pronoun points back to him, its root ġ-n-y echoes verse 8, and inna marks a fresh start at verse 12; it creates an asymmetry. | mentions 92:8, 92:12
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Verses 11–14 admonish Quraysh that God guides through revelation but does not force acceptance; they alone benefit from accepting, while both worlds remain under His control.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r3] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | prefers | Mā in verse 11 may be negative or interrogative; Islahi prefers the interrogative reading because it adds emphasis.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r4] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The wealthy are warned that wealth benefits them permanently only when spent for God and preserved for eternal life; otherwise it becomes a source of doom.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · Müfessirler | reports | Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r4] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Left to himself, a person pursues desire without regard to lawful limits, finds sin easy and pleasurable, ends in Hell, and cannot ransom himself with accumulated wealth (5:36; 70:11–16). | mentions 5:36, 70:11, 70:12, 70:13, 70:14, 70:15, 70:16
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p374/r1] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | ما يغني عنه ماله can be both a reproachful question and a negation: the wording intentionally asks what his wealth can avail and states that it will not avail him.
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p375/r1] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | The broad wording ولا تشركوا به شيئا can forbid both any object of association and any degree of shirk, whereas أحدا in the other verse specifies the meaning; كثيرا likewise allows several readings. | mentions 4:36, 18:110, 4:160
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p375/r2] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | إذا is used for events known to happen or to recur: death, the end of sacred months, sunrise, and the completion of prayer are certain examples. | mentions 5:106, 9:5, 18:17, 62:10
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p376/r1] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | When إذا and إن occur together, إذا marks the more frequent event and إن the less frequent one; across the Qur'an إذا introduces certain or common events, while إن can mark hypothetical, rare, doubtful, or impossible ones. | mentions 13:5, 5:6, 4:25, 28:71
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p376/r2] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | Tumbling into death, destruction, the grave, or Hell is certain, so if cannot replace إذا; the certainty warns misers and tyrants that wealth cannot save them.
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | The lām emphasizing God's ownership suits the surah's repeated focus on wealth and possession; unlike this context, the wealth-free context of 53:25 omits it. | mentions 53:25
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p658/r3] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | The inevitable تردّي may be death, ruin, falling into the grave, or falling into Hell; wealth will not help at that point.
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p658/r4] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | Because this end is certain, the verse warns against miserliness, oppression, and denying the good; there is no escape from it.
[STUDYQURAN:92:11/r1] STUDYQURAN · author | reports | The clause may instead be rendered as a rhetorical question asking what wealth will avail when its owner perishes.
[STUDYQURAN:92:11/r2] STUDYQURAN · IK and Ṭ | reports | “Perishes” may refer either to dying or to entering the Fire.
